Items.Authors: Sachin Joshi, Benoît Sassolas, Edoardo Cucchetti, Pierre-Antoine Frugier, Sihem Sayah, Nicolas Theret, Pierre-Alain Goulm, Christophe Latry, Matthieu Castelnau, Luis M. Gaspar Venancio, Laurent Pinard, Anne Ealet
Items.Title: Metrology of EUCLID’s dichroic plate using the observe test bench: initial PSF characterization using phase-diversity
Items.Abstract: Multilayer dichroic plates can introduce wavelength-dependent variations of the wavefront errors (WFE) and affect the point spread function (PSF) of the imaging system due to non-uniformities in its coating layers. To characterize the WFE and the PSF of the dichroic plate, a metrology test bench – OBSERVE - has been developed for the Euclid mission by Imagine Optic and is operated at Laboratoire des Matériaux Avancés (LMA), Lyon. It consists of a Shack-Hartmann (SH) sensor and a PSF imaging camera. The bench performance with measurement reproducibility within a 6-7 nm root mean square (RMS) range has already been reported. To crosscheck these results and obtain more information about the PSF, we are performing phase diversity calibration of the PSF channel. We report the preliminary results of PSF channel calibration and ongoing experimental validation, which will be used for future WFE characterization of Euclid’s dichroic spare and can be generalized to dichroic metrology studies.

Items.Authors: Anne Daumas
Items.Title: Metrology of laser interferometric benches for LISA
Items.Abstract: The LISA mission is a space-based observatory set to detect low-frequency (0.1mHz - 1Hz) gravitational waves, in a frequency band that is impossible to measure with ground-based interferometers. To achieve the required sensitivity in space through heterodyne interferometry, the optical metrology noise must be kept down to 10 pm/√Hz and the on-ground testing of the interferometric core of LISA requires the develoment of highly precise optical metrology test benches. Current work on the Optical Ground Support Equipment (OGSE) has lead to the development and characterization of critical opto-mechanical components required for fine positioning of the beams for interferometric measurements, relative alignment of the OGSE and optical bench, and performance tests.

Items.Authors: Nicholas Wenner, Joseph H. Silber, Andrew Hope, Michael Schubnell, David Schlegel, William V. Shourt, Robert Besuner
Items.Title: Miniature fiber positioning stage with planetary gear configured in a new eccentric star (“ECSTAR”) mode for 6.2 mm pitch robots
Items.Abstract: ECSTAR is a compact rotating (Φ-stage) fiber positioning mechanism for next-generation fiber-fed spectroscopic instruments, which require 2.5-3X higher packing density than current instruments like DESI. Using a planetary gearbox in "eccentric star mode," it achieves precision rotational motion within a ø5.8mm package. When coupled with a rotating θ-stage, it enables overlapping circular patrol areas for fiber robots at a 6.2 mm pitch, as envisioned for projects like SPEC-S5. Prototypes demonstrated ≤5 μm positioning precision over >180° travel range, making ECSTAR a promising candidate for future multi-object spectroscopic instruments collecting hundreds of millions of spectra.

Items.Authors: Christian Robles, Suvrath Mahadevan, Elizabeth Gonzalez, Lawrence Ramsey
Items.Title: MiraSOL: a DMD-based spectrograph for resolved solar spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: We present key upgrades to the MiraSOL instrument, an experimental spectroscopic platform utilizing a Digital Micromirror Device (DMD) for spatially resolved solar observations. The addition of a Virtual Imaged Phased Array (VIPA) spectrometer, custom DMD controller, and an improved telescope can significantly expand the science capabilities of the instrument. The VIPA increases the resolving power to 400,000, which is critical for probing subtle line shape changes. We explore a custom controller that allows precise DMD actuation, eliminating inherent duty cycling from the evaluation board and thereby increasing functional contrast. A longer focal length telescope enlarges the solar disk image projected onto the DMD surface. These enhancements provide access to the spectral characteristics of finer dynamic solar features, advancing the understanding of stellar variability—currently the most formidable challenge to precise Earth-twin detection via the radial velocity method.

Items.Authors: John C. Mather, Eliad Peretz
Items.Title: Mission design for HOEE (Hybrid Observatory for Earthlike Exoplanets)
Items.Abstract: The 39 m ELT with visible band adaptive optics, working with a 100 m diameter orbiting starshade, could image an exo-Earth at 5 pc distance in 1 minute, and get a spectrum of water and oxygen in an hour. With resolution of 3 milliarcsec, and contrast of 10^-11, detection is unambiguous. The ELT/starshade hybrid enables measurements that are otherwise impossible, for speed, resolution, and contrast. With solar electric propulsion to manage the orbit, matching velocity with the ELT, and changing orbit for each new target, we observe a target each five day orbit. With chemical propulsion, we hold alignment for hours for spectroscopy. With a new mechanical design for a 1500 kg starshade, plus supporting hardware and fuel, this mission is now possible, and could make the first detection of Earth 2.0. We present the mission concept, including mechanical design and deployment, operations, tolerances, and performance estimates.

Items.Authors: Joseph H. Silber, Nicholas Wenner, Travis Mandeville, Claire Poppett, David Schlegel
Items.Title: Modular yet connector-free fiber system for multi object spectrographs
Items.Abstract: We present a connector-free optical fiber system for multi-object spectrographs that maximizes optical throughput while enabling modular construction and simplified maintenance. The system eliminates thousands of precise fiber connections and their associated losses. To address the challenge of integrating continuous fibers across multiple subsystems with lengths reaching tens of meters, we designed 63-fiber modules that enable rapid development, testing, assembly, and repair. Key components include modular slit blocks, lightweight cabling, spool boxes for fiber management, “rafts” for integrating fiber positioning robots, and small-diameter ferrules for reversible attachment to the robots.

Items.Authors: Giuseppe De Luca, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: extended reality implementation as a tool for procedure design
Items.Abstract: The MORFEO instrument for the ELT presents significant challenges in integration, alignment, and maintenance due to its scale and complexity. To address these, an Extended Reality (XR) environment was developed with the Unity engine and deployed on a Meta Quest 3 headset. The immersive visualization enables full‑scale interaction with MORFEO’s digital model, supporting intuitive exploration of subsystems and mechanical interfaces. Compared to traditional CAD inspection, XR provides realistic spatial perception, facilitates identification of assembly conflicts, and allows rehearsal of procedures in a safe, cost‑effective setting. The paper describes the development of the Unity-based VR environment, the workflow for importing and optimizing MORFEO’s CAD models, and the interactive features implemented to support procedure design.

Items.Authors: Carmelo Arcidiacono, Francesca Annibali, Paolo Ciliegi, Elisa Portaluri, Marco Gullieuszik, Michele Cantiello
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: large-field, high-sensitivity astronomy for the ELT era
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.   By exploiting multiple lasers and natural guide stars together with several deformable mirrors conjugated to different atmospheric layers, MORFEO will deliver diffraction-limited image quality over a large, well-corrected field of view, uniform PSF and high sensitivity for the vast majority of the sky.  In this contribution, we describe the science programme crafted to maximize the scientific return of MORFEO + ELT. We present key science cases spanning deep imaging of distant galaxies, resolved stellar populations in the Milky Way and nearby galaxies, precise astrometry for dynamical studies, and time-domain observations of variable or transient objects. We outline observing strategies, expected performance, and highlight how MORFEO opens new discovery space.

Items.Authors: Marco Xompero, Nicolò Azzaroli, Matteo Tintori, Pierluigi Fumi, Lorenzo Crimella, Gabriele Clerici, Samson Sambath Kumar, Roberto Biasi
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: the deformable mirrors are ready to build!
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. The core of the MCAO correction are two Post Focal Deformable Moirros of 1m class monolithic mirrors with more than 1000 actuators for each one. The first is convex, 930 mm clear aperture while the second is concave 1224 mm clear aperture. Both DM successfully passed the Final Design Review in early 2025 and they are now in the assembly phase.

Items.Authors: Gabriele Umbriaco, Paolo Ciliegi, Andrea Comastri, Jacopo Farinato, Giuseppe Cosentino, Italo Foppiani, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Luca Marafatto, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Andrea Di Rocco, Ludovico Teodori
Items.Title: MORFEO@ELT: The Bologna Integration Hall of MORFEO, a new facility to assemble ELT-class instrumentation
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.    The newly refurbished Bologna Integration Hall (BIH) supports MORFEO’s Assembly, Integration, and Verification, enabling the alignment and calibration of its complex optical train, which features ~1-m free-form, deformable, and spherical mirrors, using high-precision metrology such as laser trackers. The facility features a 12×17×12 m ISO 8 hall, optical and electronic labs, a mechanical workshop, and a control room, all equipped with upgraded cooling, power distribution, environmental monitoring, and lifting systems under PNRR STILES investments. Ongoing upgrades include enhancements to cranes, roof insulation, external platforms, and improved networking. BIH will host MORFEO before shipment to Chile

Items.Authors: Carlos E. Rodriguez, Deibid Sebastian Leguizamón Cruz, Hector Miguel Vargas Garcia, Sergio David Montaña Cañizales
Items.Title: Multi optical fiber connector part I design
Items.Abstract: Due to the geographical location, mirror performance, and optomechanical composition of a telescope, the light spot produced in the focal plane of the celestial object being examined always varies in size. This requires a fiber optic cable with a diameter that varies depending on the telescope it is used with and the wavelengths being examined. The function of the optical fiber is to guide light from the focal plane to a spectrograph. For various reasons, several components are required, including connectors that join the fibres together or to other components.  The focus of our work is designing a multi-fibre connector for multiple fibre diameters.

Items.Authors: Ivan Zavala, Joel Castro, Mauricio Reyes, Ana De la LLata, Javier Hernández, Gerardo Sierra, Félix Diaz, Francisco Valenzuela, Luis Ortiz, Joel Herrera, Francisco Murillo, David Hiriart
Items.Title: Multi-band high-cadence imaging at OAN-SPM: design and software architecture of the 2CAN VIS–SWIR instrument
Items.Abstract: The 2CAN instrument is a dual-channel VIS–SWIR imaging system for the 1.5-m telescope at the San Pedro Mártir Observatory (OAN-SPM). It enables simultaneous high-cadence observations in the visible (400–900 nm) and short-wave infrared (950–1650 nm) using an Andor iXon 888 or Zyla 5.5 in the VIS arm and a Raptor Ninox 640 SU in the SWIR arm. A dichroic beam splitter, dual filter wheels, a VIS focusing stage, and an optical-path compensator support multi-band science, including NEO taxonomic studies, stellar occultations, and asteroid phase-curve measurements. The custom software provides synchronized camera control, a graphical interface, GPS-based timing, hardware triggering, and real-time telemetry. Bench tests confirm successful parallel imaging and the timing performance required for rapid photometry. Once deployed, 2CAN will be the first instrument at OAN-SPM capable of fast SWIR photometry, enhancing time-domain and planetary-science capabilities.

Items.Authors: John J. Hennessy, Mitchell Kallas, Fernando Cruz Aguirre, Keri Hoadley, Sarah Tuttle
Items.Title: Multilayer dielectric coatings for ultraviolet instrumentation
Items.Abstract: We describe the development of new atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes for high refractive index materials like HfF4, LaF3, and ZrF4 with the goal of utilizing them for multilayer optical coatings operating at UV wavelengths. These multilayer structures can be used in the fabrication of narrowband mirror coatings operating in the challenging far UV portion of the spectrum. Continued development in this area is of interest to a number of NASA Astrophysics applications including the smallsat concepts Maratus and UVIa. A 20-layer AlF3/LaF3 mirror coating is demonstrated and achieves an average reflectance of greater than 90% for wavelengths between 135 and 140 nm. We present the results of initial aging studies that subject these films to elevated temperature and humidity.

Items.Authors: Hanshin Lee, Uma Subash, Menelaos K. Poutous, Michael P. Smith, Brian L. Vattiat
Items.Title: Multiple-aperture grating pattern inscription engine: UV pattern lithography tool for reactive ion-plasma etched large diffraction gratings and beyond
Items.Abstract: As reported elsewhere, the Reactive Ion-PLasma Etched (RIPLE) grating technology emerged to show its highly predictive process that resulted in gratings with near theoretical super-broadband diffraction efficiency. The RIPLE process taps into electron-beam (eBeam) patterning and dry reactive-ion etching to embed a nano-scale grating structure into substrate material. Our prior NSF-supported effort succeeded in scaling the process in grating area to 4x4 sq. inch. However, our reliance on the commercially available eBeam services prevents the RIPLE process from scaling in area beyond 5x5 sq. inch. Under new NSF support, we began developing a dedicated large area grating patterning tool called the MAGPIE. It uses a long-travel nano-positioning stage and near-field Talbot effect to inscribe nano-scale grating patterns over very large areas. We discuss the operational principles, system/subsystem designs and prototyping activities so far, and some of the early tests of the MAGPIE.

Items.Authors: Sapir Lazar, Alexander Telle
Items.Title: Multiscale stray-light control for large astronomy and space telescopes
Items.Abstract: Stray-light suppression is a key limitation in both spaceborne instruments and large astronomical telescopes, where grazing-incidence reflections and uncontrolled background illumination degrade imaging performance. This work presents a multiscale light-trapping architecture that provides a compact, vane-free alternative to traditional baffle designs. The structure integrates macro-scale hexagonal cells, micro-scale metallic foils, and nano-scale ultra-black coatings to drive photons into sequential high-loss interactions. Experimental BRDF measurements and system-level simulations across visible and infrared wavelengths demonstrate strongly diffusive scattering and order-of-magnitude reductions in integrated stray light. The approach offers a scalable solution for next-generation telescopes, star trackers, and precision optical instruments requiring lightweight, maintenance-free stray-light suppression.

Items.Authors: Hugues Sana, Bart Vandenbussche, Gert Raskin, Emilie Beevers, Pierre Royer
Items.Title: MUSTI: a Massive star far-Ultraviolet Spectroscopic TIme domain mission
Items.Abstract: With a 40 cm-aperture, MUSTI is a far-ultraviolet (FUV) spectroscopic ESA F-class mission proposal dedicated to time-domain stellar physics. MUSTI combines a tailor-made, high-resolution (R = 20 000), FUV (120-210 nm) échelle spectrograph and a secondary high precision pointing system with a standardised platform. MUSTI will obtain breakthrough  observational constraints on massive stars’ interior physics, stellar winds and binary products.  These novel constraints will enable the precise calibration of the evolution of massive single  and binary stars towards their final fate, with far reaching implications for cosmic models,  the interpretation of the first stars and the first galaxies observed by the James Webb Space  Telescope and inference-based analyses of Gravitational Waves detections.

Items.Authors: Anand Nagesh
Items.Title: Nano-Observatory-as-a-Service (NOaaS): a constellation of suitcase sized CubeSat telescopes for near real-time 3D sky mapping and anomaly detection using AWS-Integrated Professional service to enable virtual observatories
Items.Abstract: Nano Observatory as a Service (NOaaS):A Cloud-Connected Space/Ground Telescope Network for Real-Time Sky Awareness is a new way of monitoring the sky, using a fleet of small telescopes in space, combined with ground observatories and cloud computing on aws, to deliver real-time insights about what is happening above Earth. Instead of relying only on large, expensive observatories, NOaaS uses multiple compact telescopes in low-Earth orbit working together as a virtual global observatory.  In the age of AI and computing we are building a future by transforming how humanity explores space by monetizing access to cosmic events through Leveraging Space/Ground data from network of multispectral ground and In-Orbit Telescopes with accurate AI models for astronomy, education, and Asset/SSA-adjacent space mapping for making it accessible to researchers, students, space asset operators, Insurance company and enthusiasts worldwide using AWS platform.

Items.Authors: Kumiko Morihana, Ichi Tanaka, Shogo Nishiyama
Items.Title: New narrow-band filter system on MOIRCS at the Subaru Telescope
Items.Abstract: Narrow-band imaging can identify emission and absorption features from many sources simultaneously, but continuum subtraction becomes difficult when spectral slopes vary or when equivalent widths are small. We developed a new narrow-band filter set for MOIRCS on the Subaru Telescope that includes a main Br-gamma passband (wavelength center: 2.168 microns, width:0.016 microns) and additional passbands (wavelength center: 2.139, 2.214 microns, width:0.023, 0.018 microns) on both sides of the line. This design enables more accurate continuum estimation than conventional filters that transmit only on one side. On-sky tests confirm that the new system can detect emission lines with small equivalent widths that are often missed by traditional narrow-band imaging. We present the filter design and its demonstrated performance.

Items.Authors: Vincenzo Davide Cardinale, Alfonso Collura, Andrea Bocchieri, Paolo Chioetto, Riccardo Claudi, Elisa Guerriero, Alberto Gulizzi, Riccardo Lilli, Giuseppe Malaguti, Giuseppina Micela, Emanuele Pace, Enzo Pascale, Paolo Picchi, Giampaolo Preti, Claudio Saitta, Antonio Scippa, Andrea Tozzi, Salvatore Varisco, Paola Zuppella, Fabio D’Anca
Items.Title: Non-destructive dynamic characterization of thin Ni-P coatings on Ariel AW6061-T651 mirrors using modal analysis
Items.Abstract: This work presents a non-destructive modal analysis approach for the dynamic characterization of thin Ni-P optical coatings developed for the ESA Ariel mission. Experimental tests on coated aluminum substrates demonstrate that the technique is highly sensitive to coating properties, enabling accurate evaluation of their impact on natural frequencies, mode shapes, and damping. The method provides a complete dynamic fingerprint without altering the sample, supporting coating thickness assessment, FEM model validation, and detection of anisotropic effects. These results contribute to the optimization of high-precision mirror systems, ultimately enhancing Ariel’s capability to deliver accurate spectroscopic data for exoplanet atmosphere studies.

Items.Authors: Alexander Pevtsov, Luca Bertello
Items.Title: NSOs full disk MOF based vector magnetograph concept (MVMC)
Items.Abstract: The Sun's magnetic field serves as the primary driver of solar eruptions. Precise and uninterrupted measurement of the Sun’s magnetic fields are required for predictions of solar eruptive phenomena and evaluating their potential impact on the Earth and on space missions. The primary instrument used by the majority of space weather agencies is NSF's NSO's Global Oscillations Network Group (GONG). GONG employs a modest effective aperture and is only capable of generating line-of-sight (LOS) magnetograms. There are a number of efforts to create networks of Magneto-Optical Filter (MOF) based LOS magnetographs (SAMNet, GATES). However, vector magnetographs have a number of advantages and are the future of the field. The proposed instrument will be capable of continuously producing vector magnetograms. An instrument such this could be used for both groundbased and satellite observatories thus allowing for multi-messenger style missions. We discuss the instrument design and its capabilities.

Items.Authors: Derya Öztürk Çetni, Cahit Yeşilyaprak, Jonas Kühn
Items.Title: Numerical investigation of NCP - induced coronagraphic performance for DAG400 telescope
Items.Abstract: This work presents a detailed numerical study of how alignment errors and residual aberrations shape the coronagraphic performance of the 4-meter Eastern Anatolia Observatory (DAG) Telescope. The analysis concentrates on non-common-path (NCP) aberrations, slow mechanical drifts along the optical train, focal-plane mask offsets, Lyot stop misplacements, and shifts introduced during pupil-tracking operation. Together, these effects determine the structure of the final point-spread function and the contrast that can be reached at the near-infrared (NIR) detector.    To examine these contributions in a controlled environment, a Python-based simulation tool - the DAG Coronagraph Numerical Simulator (NoDC) - was developed. Relying on diffraction propagation and a full coronagraphic model, the framework follows how small misalignments evolve through the system and how residual wavefront errors from the active optics (ao) and adaptive optics (AO) stages imprint themselves on the science images.

Items.Authors: Joschua Hellemeier
Items.Title: Numerical simulations on the feasibility of polychromatic laser guide stars
Items.Abstract: Polychromatic laser guide stars are one suggested method for tip/tilt retrieval without the use of a natural guide star in adaptive optics systems. For polychromatic laser guide stars, sodium atoms are excited to upper energy levels, use different decay channels to the ground state, and emit light at different wavelengths. Due to dispersion, the light at different wavelengths will show small differences in tip/tilt after propagating through the atmosphere. This differential tip/tilt component can be used to retrieve the total tip/tilt in an adaptive optics system.   We study the feasibility of polychromatic laser guide stars for tip/tilt retrieval by using optical Bloch equations to simulate the excitation of sodium in the mesosphere and by using physical optics to model the propagation of light through the atmosphere.

Items.Authors: Mackenzie F. Carlson, Stephan R. McCandliss, Emily Witt, Jack Ford, Alexander S. Kutyrev, Suryakanthi Srinivas Rachamadugu, Kyowon Kim, Meng-Ping Chang, Paul A. Scowen, Edward J. Wollack
Items.Title: OAxFORTIS far-UV sounding rocket observations of hot stars in globular cluster M10
Items.Abstract: The Off-Axis Far-UV Off Rowland-circle Telescope for Imaging and Spectroscopy (OAxFORTIS) is an off-axis reconfiguration of the sounding rocket experiment, FORTIS, designed to conduct multi-object spectroscopy. OAxFORTIS enables the investigation of the UV diversity of the hot horizontal branch (HHB) in the otherwise similar globular clusters M10, M13, and M3. This exploration is intended to address a question commonly referred to as the "Second Parameter Problem" as researchers hunt for parameters other than metallicity that drive this diversity. The first flight of OAxFORTIS took place on August 2024 and resulted in the successful observation of M10, with at least 3 strong stellar spectra acquired. Preparations for the second launch include the installation of XeLIF optical coatings and a new Next Generation microshutter array. We report on the observational results from the first flight and the pre-flight preparations for the second launch.

Items.Authors: Kenji Emerson, Adwin Boogert, Mike Connelley, John Rayner, Charles Lockhart
Items.Title: Observation simulations of the IRTF SPECTRE spectrograph
Items.Abstract: We present an observation simulator for the SPECTRE spectrograph. SPECTRE is an upcoming, low resolution, broad bandwidth (0.4-4.2 μm), 7.2” field-of-view, three channel, Integral Field Unit (IFU) spectrograph for the NASA Infrared Telescope Facility (IRTF). It is designed for characterizing near-Earth asteroids and spectroscopic follow-up on astrophysical transients. A facility-ready data reduction pipeline is integral to its use by astronomers. We comprehensively simulate observations, accounting for transmissive, emissive, and dispersive effects from the atmosphere, telescope, instrument optics, prisms, and the detector. Instrument calibrations, flat-fielding lamps and spectral arc lamps, can also be simulated. We use our simulations for the on-going development of the SPECTRE data reduction suite, and it can also be used as an exposure time calculator for astronomers to optimize their observing session.

Items.Authors: Evgeniy A. Kopylov, Michael Sachkov, Sergey Sichevsky, Yuriy Kazakevich
Items.Title: On the ground support facilities of the Spektr-UF mission
Items.Abstract: Observational data in the ultraviolet region of the electromagnetic spectrum (115-305 nm) are a powerful tool for studying many astrophysical objects, such as exoplanets, especially for determining the characteristics of their atmospheres. Work is underway to create the Spektr-UV orbital space Observatory (World Space Observatory - Ultraviolet), which will succeed the Hubble Space Telescope. The Institute of Astronomy of the Russian Academy of Sciences is the leading scientific organization of this project. Within the framework of this study, work is planned to determine the characteristics for creating instruments for ground support of missions, to develop tools for preparing applications for an observation program, and to develop a scientific research program for the project.

Items.Authors: Simone Chiarucci, Andrea Russi, Giovanni Giusi, Mauro Focardi, Anna Maria Di Giorgio, Rosario Cosentino, Marina Vela Nunez, Pierpaolo Merola, Scigè John Liù
Items.Title: On-board control procedures for autonomous alignment of science production and hardware compression for the PLATO Mission
Items.Abstract: The PLATO mission requires twenty-four Normal Cameras (NCAMs) to operate coherently for high-precision photometry. To prevent data stream corruption, the Instrument Control Unit (ICU) must align data production to a strict 6.25s acquisition slot. This paper presents a specialized On-Board Control Procedure (OBCP) designed to manage this synchronization. We describe the nominal start-up sequence, utilizing a reference NCAM event to trigger simultaneous observation and hardware compression, ensuring phase coherence. Furthermore, we detail the autonomous FDIR logic executed following an ICU reboot at the L2 Lagrange point. This sequence restores the Payload Configuration Vector (PCV) and re-initializes N-DPUs to re-establish valid data chunking without ground support. Implemented via interpreted OCL scripts, this architecture allows for dynamic decision-making and in-flight updates. We demonstrate how this flexibility ensures robust fault recovery, minimizing scientific downtime.

Items.Authors: John T. Rayner, Mike Connelley, Adwin Boogert, Kenji Emerson, Mike Kelii, Dan Kokubun, Charles Lockhart, Jim Thorne
Items.Title: One-shot 0.4-4.2-micron integral field R=250 spectrograph and imager for the NASA IRTF
Items.Abstract: SPECTRE is a new low-resolution (R≈250) integral-field spectrograph and imager that provides continuous 0.4–4.2 μm wavelength coverage in a single exposure. Built at the University of Hawai’i for first light on the 3.2-m IRTF in 2028, its science drivers include rapid characterization of NEOs, small solar system bodies, and optical-infrared transients.  The instrument uses two dichroics to split the beam into optical, near-IR, and mid-IR channels feeding a 2k×2k frame-transfer CCD and two H2RG arrays, all operated by Archon controllers. A 7.2″×7.2″ image-slicer IFU provides slit-loss-free spectroscopy, and each channel employs a mirror-based collimator-camera with dual-pass prisms. For stability the bench-mounted optics and arrays contain no moving parts. The optics and arrays are cryogenically cooled by one closed-cycle cooler.   Acquisition and guiding use a 3′×3′ warm CCD camera, with optional on-object near-IR guiding from rapid H2RG reads. We summarize the design and status.

Items.Authors: Qihang Zhang, Guifeng Chen, Shuangquan Chen, Yonggang Gu, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: Online upgradeable fiber positioning drive system for LAMOST
Items.Abstract: The LAMOST improvement project has entered a critical phase, with a new generation of integrated fiber positioning robots set to replace half of the fiber positioning units on the focal plane. This paper designs a drive system for the three-in-one fiber positioning robot. Featuring a compact hardware layout, it utilizes a Type-C interface that multiplexes power supply, communication, and programming functions, with main dimensions of 140mm × 10mm. Software-wise, a CAN communication protocol is established to process commands, with motors controlled via SVPWM subdivision drive. CAN enables IAP (In Application Programming), allowing online firmware upgrades for the drive board without disassembly or power interruption after installation on the focal plane. Testing within the LAMOST fiber positioning system demonstrates positioning accuracy below 10 micrometers. The online upgrade capability also enhances the efficiency and convenience of LAMOST's future upgrades and maintenance.

Items.Authors: Jin-Ah Kim, Haeun Chung, Miriam Keppler, Aafaque Khan, Carlos Vargas, Erika Hamden
Items.Title: On-orbit calibration plan for the Aspera FUV SmallSat
Items.Abstract: Aspera is a SmallSat mission funded by the NASA Astrophysics Pioneers program. Aspera will be launched in 2026 and is designed to observe diffuse O VI emission at 103.2nm from the circumgalactic medium of nearby galaxies. The payload consists of two long-slit spectrographs with a field of view of 1 degree by 40 arcsec. We have developed calibration methods to measure astrometric solutions, dispersion relationships, spectral and spatial resolution, and effective area curves using on-orbit observations. In our presentation, we will describe our observational plans and analysis strategies for the calibration.

Items.Authors: Anna Brucalassi, Giuliano Pignata, José Antonio Araiza-Duran, Matteo Aliverti, Federico Battaini, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Simone Di Filippo, Davide Ricci, Mirko Colapietro, Matteo Munari, Pietro Schipani, Sergio Campana, Paolo D'Avanzo
Items.Title: On-site integration and commissioning for the Acquisition and Guiding System of SOXS
Items.Abstract: The Son Of X-Shooter (SOXS) is a single-object spectroscopic facility for the ESO-NTT 3.6-m telescope. It consists of two high-efficiency spectrograph arms that together cover the 350–2050 nm spectral range with an average resolving power of R≈4500.The instrument is undergoing to the commissioning phase.     This paper presents the opto-mechanical on-site reintegration and alignment control of the SOXS Acquisition and Guiding System following its shipment to La Silla Observatory. It also reports and discusses the results of the functional and optical performance verification carried out during the commissioning runs, along with its first on-sky characterization.

Items.Authors: Zhengjiang Zhang, Huatao Zhang, Yanbing Chen, Tong Zhou, Kai Zhang, Mingda Jiang, Zhen Tang
Items.Title: On-site integration and commissioning of a high-resolution echelle spectrograph for the 1.2m astronomical telescope of Sun Yat-Sen University
Items.Abstract: The astronomical high dispersion spectrograph for the 1.2-meter astronomical telescope is a fiber-fed, high-resolution echelle spectrograph located at the astronomical station of Zhuhai campus of Sun Yat-Sen University. It is fed by the Cassegrain focus via a 25-meter-long, 2.7’’ optical fiber. The spectrograph provides spectral resolution higher than 30000 over the wavelength range of 400-900nm. It enables the science team to do frontier researches and education in astronomical fields such as chemical element abundance measurement, stellar formation and evolution. This paper mainly describes the spectrograph alignment and the commissioning performance. We adopted a method of combining autocollimation with Knife-Edge test to intuitively and precisely align the optical axis of each optical component, and improve working efficiency. With the commissioning observations, the instrumental performance has been further optimized and met the scientific requirements.

Items.Authors: Mirko Colapietro, Sergio D'Orsi, Salvatore Savarese, Pietro Schipani, Laurent Marty, Giulio Capasso, Ricardo Zanmar Sánchez, Kalyan Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Federico Battaini, Simone Di Filippo, Matteo Aliverti, Simone Doniselli, Andrea Baruffolo, Davide Ricci, Bernardo Salasnich, Paolo D'Avanzo, Sergio Campana, Riccardo Claudi, David Young, Marco Landoni, Matteo Munari, Stephen Smartt, Matteo Genoni, Fabrizio Vitali, Salvatore Scuderi, Rosario Cosentino, Frédéric Dérie, Markus Schoeller, Armin Silber, Ivo Saviane, Emanuela Pompei, Derek Ives, Antonio Miccichè, Gaetano Nicotra, Eugenio Martinetti, Silvio Di Rosa, Marco Dima, Adam Rubin, Marco Riva, Michael Rappaport, Giuliano Pignata, Luigi Lessio, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Ofir Hershko, Francesco D'Alessio, Anna Brucalassi, Alex Bichkovsky, Sagi Ben-Ami, José Antonio Araiza-Durán, Maximilian Stritzinger, Seppo Mattila, Avishay Gal-Yam, Iair Arcavi, Massimo Della Valle, Enrico Cappellaro
Items.Title: On-site integration and validation of the SOXS control electronics at ESO-NTT
Items.Abstract: The Son Of X-Shooter (SOXS) instrument is a dual-arm, wide-band spectrograph designed to provide rapid and flexible follow-up observations of transient phenomena with the ESO NTT.  After successfully completing its Preliminary Acceptance in Europe at the end of 2024, the instrument was shipped to the ESO La Silla Observatory.  This paper presents the on-site integration and validation of the SOXS control electronics.  We describe the tests performed at the telescope, including hardware integration, verification of network and software interfaces, functional checks of the motion and thermal control systems, and communication tests with the instrument control software.  Particular emphasis is placed on the assessment of timing stability, electromagnetic compatibility within the telescope environment, and system robustness under operational constraints such as temperature variations and safety interlocks, highlighting lessons learned that guided the optimization of the system.

Items.Authors: Aditi Desai, Stephanie E. Sallum, Andrew J. Skemer
Items.Title: On-sky demonstration of speckle noise removal using the SCALES medium-spectral-resolution mode
Items.Abstract: The Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy (SCALES) is a 2-5 micron high-contrast lenslet-based integral field spectrograph (IFS) designed to detect and characterize exoplanets. The SCALES medium-resolution mode comprises a lenslet subarray with a 0.34 x 0.36 arcsecond field of view (FOV) and an image slicer, allowing for measurements of molecular abundances and disequilibrium chemistry in giant exoplanet atmospheres at increased spectral resolution. This mode uses a piezo-electric mirror to offset the FOV from the star to the planet. We use SCALES commissioning data to perform tests on speckle noise removal software designed specifically for observations this mode, employing angular and spectral differential imaging to mitigate stellar, atmospheric, and instrumental noise effects. We demonstrate the achievable contrast for the medium-resolution mode and use the results to estimate our ability to recover planet signals and characterize exoplanet atmospheres.

Items.Authors: Roland Winkler, Weijia Sun, Scott Smedley, Daniel Sablowski, Thomas Szeifert, Diogo Rio Fernandes, Ingo Stilz, Alexander Pramskiy, Gerard Zins, Ole Streicher, Thomas Liebner, Steffen Frey
Items.Title: On-sky fibre-target-alignment of the 4MOST instrument: calibration and performance
Items.Abstract: The 4-metre Multi-Object Spectroscopic Telescope (4MOST) is a new wide-field, fibre-fed spectroscopic survey facility for the VISTA telescope at ESO’s Paranal Observatory. The instrument enables the simultaneous acquisition of 2436 spectra across a 4.2 deg² field of view, using a tilting spine fibre positioner feeding three dedicated spectrographs. In this paper, we describe the final calibration process, and performance verification of the Fibre-Target-Alignment (FTA) for 4MOST on the VISTA telescope. We show how reach a final positioning performance of approximately 10um / 0.16 arc sec relative to targets on sky.

Items.Authors: Elena Tonucci, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Warren B. Foster, Jared R. Males, Olivier Guyon, Laird M. Close, Kyle Van Gorkom, Alexander D. Hedglen, Parker T. Johnson, Maggie Y. Kautz, Jay K. Kueny, Rico Landman, Jialin Li, Joshua Liberman, Joseph D. Long, Miles Lucas, Jennifer Lumbres, Matthijs Mars, Eden A. McEwen, Avalon McLeod, Tiffany Nguyen, Logan A. Pearce, María Eugenia Redondo González, Lauren Schatz, Katie Twitchell
Items.Title: On-sky imaging of faint companions at the diffraction limit with nano-printed PIAACMC coronagraphic focal plane masks
Items.Abstract: The extreme contrast and small separations needed to image Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zones cannot be reached with current technology. The Phase-Induced Amplitude Apodization Complex Mask Coronagraph (PIAACMC) is a promising device to reach this goal. With its aspheric lenses to losslessly apodize the entrance pupil and a phase-shifting focal plane mask for starlight suppression, it allows us to achieve high throughput and small inner-working angle (IWA). The masks are manufactured in-house at Leiden University with Nanoscribe, a micro-3D-printer that uses two-photon polymerization achieving submicron precision in height.  We present the first on-sky performance results of the PIAACMC at visible wavelengths and the detection of faint companions at separations 1-4λ/D (30-120mas) with MagAO-X, the extreme adaptive optics instrument for the 6.5m Magellan Clay telescope at Las Campanas Observatory. This demonstrates the PIAACMC’s capability to observe at the diffraction limit.

Items.Authors: Beth Garton, Iain A. Steele, Helen E. Jermak, Chloe Miossec, Stuart D. Bates
Items.Title: On-sky rapid prototyping of the Squash spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The New Robotic Telescope (NRT) will be a 4-metre class fully autonomous telescope on La Palma. Its instrumentation suite builds on that of the Liverpool Telescope (LT) with a range of low-cost, reliable instruments that are easily maintained. Squash will be NRT’s flagship spectrograph; designed for the rapid classification of galactic and extragalactic transient and variable events. The LT, and its future partner facility the NRT, are autonomous telescopes with limited human access; these facilities require no-fuss instrumentation, which are all co-mounted at the telescope Cassegrain focus. Many of the current LT instrumentation suite are designed with moving parts; although these have proven to be reliable, the presence of moving parts makes failure more likely. Thus, to increase reliability and lower maintenance requirements, we have completed research and development for a low-resolution spectrograph with no moving parts.

Items.Authors: Mayra Gutierrez, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Steph Sallum, Charlotte Guthery, Antonin Bouchez, Maïssa Salama, Mahawa Cissé, Katherine de Kleer
Items.Title: On-sky science verification of Keck Observatory's HAKA adaptive optics upgrade
Items.Abstract: Early in 2026, Keck Observatory will upgrade its adaptive optics system to feature a 2844-actuator deformable mirror as part of the High-Order All-Sky Keck Adaptive Optics project (HAKA). To characterize HAKA’s on-sky performance, we evaluate its K-band Strehl ratio as a function of guide-star magnitude using NIRC2, and compare these results to Strehl ratios obtained with the previous 349-actuator system. We further evaluate HAKA’s performance through z-band observations of Solar System objects and by measuring achievable contrast curves with NIRC2. Since Keck Observatory will also be integrating the Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy (SCALES) in 2026, we will repeat these on-sky HAKA observations with SCALES, as available. Together, these measurements will provide the first comprehensive on-sky assessment of HAKA’s science capabilities and inform the planetary science and high-contrast exoplanet imaging programs enabled by the upgraded Keck AO system.

Items.Authors: Jessica B. Patel, Razia Khan Sharme, Luis Rodriguez de Marcos, Javier G. Del Hoyo, Manuel A. Quijada, Mukti M. Rana
Items.Title: Optical and electrical response of transparent conductive multilayer coatings under humidity exposure
Items.Abstract: Transparent conductive multilayer coatings based on TiO₂/SiOₓ/ITO are of interest for space optical systems operating at 1064 nm, a wavelength widely used in laser ranging, LiDAR, and near-infrared instrumentation. In space environments, optical components can accumulate electrostatic charge due to plasma exposure and radiation, potentially degrading optical performance. Incorporating transparent conductive layers enables passive charge dissipation while maintaining high transmission. In this work, the optical and electrical response of TiO₂/SiOₓ/ITO multilayer coatings was evaluated under controlled humidity exposure. Reflectance and transmittance spectra were measured from clear and frosted surfaces across 400–2000 nm. Apparent transmittance at 1064 nm reaches ~96–99% for the best-performing sample before and after exposure, indicating stable optical performance, while electrical measurements show increased sheet resistance after humidity exposure.

Items.Authors: Matias Marambio-Jimenez, Luca Antonucci, Mauricio Flores, Leonardo Vanzi, Takeo Minezaki, Kentaro Motohara
Items.Title: Optical and opto-mechanical design of the Tao Aiuc high resolution Y-band spectrograph front-end and its expected AO performance
Items.Abstract: The University of Tokyo Atacama Observatory (TAO) offers exceptional conditions for infrared astronomy. However, the efficiency of the TAO AIUC High-Resolution Y-band Spectrograph (TARdYS) is limited by atmospheric turbulence. A significant mismatch between the site’s median seeing and the instrument's optical fiber aperture results in substantial photon loss. This research presents the design and prototyping of a commercial-off-the-shelf optical front-end aimed at mitigating these losses through an adaptive optics system. The project involved end-to-end simulations, the fabrication of a custom wavefront sensor, and the construction of a laboratory prototype. While the system successfully corrected static optical errors to be diffraction-limite, dynamic tests highlighted engineering challenges regarding linearity and hysteresis. This work validates optical design and identifies the critical hardware integrations necessary for the commissioning of the TARdYS instrument.

Items.Authors: Alexis Hill, Glen Herriot, Thushara Gunaratne, Zoran Ljusic, Scott Macdonald, Emma Rautio-Roe, William Thompson, Maaike van Kooten, Ross Cheriton, Siegfried Janz, Brent Carlson, Leonid Belostotski, John Nielsen, Peter Shmerko
Items.Title: Optical aperture synthesis: lab demonstration of adaptive optics using integrated photonics without deformable mirrors or wavefront sensors
Items.Abstract: The Optical Aperture Synthesis (OAS) pathfinder project aims to advance adaptive optics by replacing traditional deformable mirrors and wavefront sensors with a fiber-fed integrated photonic chip capable of rapid phase control and beam combination. A laboratory demonstration shows H-band light from four fiber-fed channels combined on-chip with closed-loop phase correction, achieving an order of magnitude faster response than conventional systems. Future work will retrofit the demonstrator to a 1.2 m telescope for on-sky testing, paving the way eventually for arrays of small telescopes that may achieve micro-arcsecond resolution in near-infrared imaging and spectroscopy of exoplanets.

Items.Authors: Lorenz Wilmen, Dane Zielinski-Nicolson, Michael Weber, Christian Schwab, Julian Stürmer, Daniel Sablowski, Jacob Pember, Thomas Legero, David Coutts
Items.Title: Optical characterisation and modelling of a UV-Vis Fabry-Perot Etalon for wavelength calibration of EPRV spectrometers
Items.Abstract: Stable broadband Fabry–Pérot etalons are essential calibrators for extreme-precision radial-velocity (EPRV) spectrographs, providing dense, uniform reference spectra with the line symmetry, smoothness, and long-term stability required to achieve centimeter-per-second sensitivity. Such etalons must deliver high throughput and moderate finesse, while the desired stability requires fiber-coupled operation in temperature-controlled vacuum enclosures. The ultimate spectral stability and uniformity of these devices are governed by the mirror coatings, cavity substrate figure, and geometric precision, with secondary contributions from the illumination optics. We are developing a prototype broadband etalon for the U- to V-band calibration channels of the ANDES spectrometer at the ELT. In this contribution, we present high-precision metrology of the optical surfaces and compare these measurements with end-to-end simulations of the resulting etalon spectra.

Items.Authors: Nitish Singh
Items.Title: Optical design of a direct fibre-fed mos for the 2.34 m VBT
Items.Abstract: We are designing the optical system of a direct fiber-fed, multi-object, medium-resolution spectrograph for the 2.34 m Vainu Bappu Telescope (VBT). The instrument will simultaneously accept light from 100 optical fibers placed at the telescope’s prime-focus focal plane, which provides a native f/3 beam. Each fiber has a core diameter of 100 µm and feeds an f/3 beam directly into the spectrograph, eliminating the need for a traditional entrance slit and improving throughput. The spectrograph operates in two channels—blue (350–620 nm) and red (600–1000 nm)—to provide continuous wavelength coverage across the optical band. The design targets a resolving power of R ≈ 3000 in both channels. The expected image quality delivers a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 2–3 pixels on the detector, where one pixel corresponds to 24 µm. This ensures adequate sampling and stable spectral performance across the full field

Items.Authors: Jason R. Fucik, Richard Dekany, Jeb Bailey, Dan Reiley
Items.Title: Optical design of Z-Shooter: a broadband (20,000A) intermediate resolution high-efficiency spectrometer
Items.Abstract: An optical design for a 3-channel cross-dispersed echelle spectrometer operating from the NUV to NIR for the W.M. Keck Observatory. The spectrometer covers 20,000A in a single exposure with intermediate resolution of 20,000 for single-object spectroscopy. Designed for rapid response automated target acquisition and real-time reduction and display of acquired spectra.

Items.Authors: Charles Lee, Tyrone E. Woods, Patrick Côté, John S. Pazder
Items.Title: Optical modelling of a digital micromirror device as programmable slits for the CASTOR ultraviolet multi-object spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The Ultraviolet Multi-Object Spectrograph (UVMOS) is a proposed UV (150 to 300 nm) instrument for the CASTOR mission. The UVMOS utilizes a digital micromirror device (DMD) to create object selecting slits. The DMD consists of programmable mirrors that tilt +/- 12 degrees to selectively project the incoming field to a collecting aperture. Multi-object spectroscopy using the DMD has been demonstrated in the optical and infrared and is being evaluated for future UV missions like CASTOR and HWO. This work builds on previous simulations of a DLP7000 device in the UV using electromagnetic finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method to understand its optical performance. We introduce new results alongside additions to our FDTD model that simulates the underlying substrate and manufacturing-induced surface defects. We quantify the DMD efficiency and contrast in the UVMOS operating wavelengths (150 to 300 nm) and discuss how that leads to constraints to optical design of the UVMOS.

Items.Authors: Walter Rahmer, Christopher Walker, Aman Chandra, Heejoo Choi, Daewook Kim, Hina Suzuki, Adrien Bouskela
Items.Title: Optics and instruments for far-infrared space telescopes with inflatable primary reflectors
Items.Abstract: Advancing the exploration of astronomical phenomena in the far-infrared band will require larger aperture instruments to enable higher angular resolutions and increased light-collecting ability. Recent developments in inflatable structures offer a promising low mass and volume solution, allowing large concave reflective surfaces to be carried by smaller spacecraft.   This work will leverage related experimental results for membrane structures, presenting a study of corrective optics to compensate for the aspheric pressure driven reflector shape. The proposed design is then evaluated for its stability and its tolerance to low-order aberrations and errors in membrane shape. A prototype optical system is built for a 3m diameter inflatable primary optic, and its performance is evaluated for wavefront quality at far-IR frequencies. From these results the expected performance of an 8 meter aperture telescope is shown.

Items.Authors: Justin Vella, Barnaby Norris, Sergio Leon-Saval, Chris Betters, Jin Wei, Adam Taras, Joss Bland-Hawthorn, Andrew Ross-Adams
Items.Title: Optimal design of application-specific photonic lanterns using Bayesian optimisation
Items.Abstract: Photonic lanterns (PLs) are gaining interest for focal-plane wavefront sensing and other applications, yet their design remains largely trial-and-error and heuristic-based, with little prior control of the transfer function before fabrication. Here we present a numerical optimization framework using Bayesian optimization for PL design. This enables specific, novel device properties – such as hybrid-mode-selective PLs (HMS-PLs) – to be defined and achieved using well-tested algorithms. In this example, at each iteration the algorithm tunes the physical parameters defining the PL’s central core, computes the complex transfer matrix, and compares its behaviour with the desired functionality (e.g. an ideal HMS-PL) to produce a loss value for the next iteration. The resulting optimization record also enables estimation of the underlying probability density function and visualization of parameter co-dependencies, providing a maximum-likelihood estimate for achieving hybrid-mode selectivity.

Items.Authors: Kaining Yang, He Sun
Items.Title: Optimal design of shaped pupil Lyot coronagraph for China's large segmented-aperture telescopes
Items.Abstract: China's next-generation large telescopes aim for high-angular-resolution exoplanet imaging. However, their segmented, centrally obscured apertures present coronagraph challenges, especially for high contrast at small inner working angles. We propose an optimized Shaped Pupil Lyot Coronagraph (SPLC) with a binary shaped pupil apodizer, occulting mask, and Lyot stop, enhanced by a two-deformable-mirror (2DM) adaptive optics system for atmospheric correction. Our design achieves contrasts better than 1×10-10 at 2.5 λ/D in ideal conditions, and simulations for Lenghu in Qinghai show better than 1×10⁻6 in the V, H, and K bands. This performance exceeds existing ground-based coronagraphs, making the 2DM-SPLC a strong candidate for China's future large telescopes.

Items.Authors: Teodor Malendevych, Barnaby Norris, Christopher Betters, Andrew Ross-Adams, Olivier Guyon, Sergio Leon-Saval
Items.Title: Optimal single-mode injection of distorted PSFs: matched electric field optimisation using a photonic lantern
Items.Abstract: Fiber-fed astrophotonic instruments depend on coupling light into single-mode fibres (SMF). Imperfect point spread  functions (PSFs) degrade coupling efficiency due to mode field mismatch. For post-coronagraphic imaging, reduced  planet light coupling and increased stellar speckle can decrease SNR by an order of magnitude. We present a method  to actively match a multimode fibre’s (MMF) mode field to any PSF using a photonic lantern that maps the MMF  into single-mode waveguides with active phase and amplitude modulation. Operating in reverse (SMF-to-MMF),  we optimise to a predetermined mode profile using Stochastic Parallel Gradient Descent. Switching to forward  operation achieves optimal injection. Multimode interference couplers recombine science light into one SMF. We  compare simulated coupling efficiency for 3×1, 7×1 and 19×1 lanterns versus bare SMF, demonstrate in-lab results,  and present applications to the Matched Electric Field Spectrograph for Habitable Worlds Observatory

Items.Authors: Claude J. Aime, Simon Prunet, Céline Theys-Ferrari
Items.Title: Optimization of petal-shaped occulters for exo-Earth observation
Items.Abstract: Petal-shaped occulters are giant, formation-flying optical devices designed for use in space astronomy.     This study focuses on optimizing the shape of the occulter in order to significantly reduce Fresnel diffraction, which, in the case of a simple circular occulter, would manifest itself as an Arago spot comparable to the pupil of the telescope. Nevertheless, we will construct an occulter as the weighted sum of circular occulters such that the contribution of the complex amplitudes of the corresponding Arago spots is minimized over the telescope aperture.  This basis of circular occulters allows the use of a simple analytical form for their Fresnel diffraction. The weights are then obtained by minimizing a quadratic criterion.

Items.Authors: Julien Storm, Gert Raskin, Bart Vandenbussche, Hugues Sana, Dirk Vandepitte, Leonardo Peri, Sibo Van Gool, Louis Storm, Pierre Royer, Maddalena Reggiani, Camille Pirat, Jorg Versluys, Mathijs Arts
Items.Title: Optomechanical design, alignment and characterization of the CubeSpec high-resolution cross-dispersed echelle slit spectrograph
Items.Abstract: CubeSpec is a 12U CubeSat mission designed to demonstrate high-resolution spectroscopy from a compact platform. The mission is now in construction phase with launch readiness early 2027. The payload is built around a cross-dispersed echelle spectrograph, achieving a resolving power of R≈55,000 throughout the visible wavelength range. We present here the optomechanical design, alignment, and characterization of the CubeSpec spectrograph, with a focus on validating its performance within the severe volume constraints imposed by a CubeSat platform. Characterization encompasses spectral response, which is assessed through simulations of the resolving power, order separation, wavelength coverage and a detailed analysis of the slit image.
